title: Add more `opt_*()` functions
description:
These additional `opt_*()` functions provide convenient ways to set multiple table options for typical styling activities.

Here are some examples of the new functions:

```r
library(gt)

tab_1 <-
  exibble %>%
  gt(rowname_col = "row", groupname_col = "group") %>%
  summary_rows(
    groups = "grp_a",
    columns = vars(num, currency),
    fns = list(
      min = ~min(., na.rm = TRUE),
      max = ~max(., na.rm = TRUE)
    )) %>%
  grand_summary_rows(
    columns = vars(currency),
    fns = list(
      total = ~sum(., na.rm = TRUE)
    )) %>%
  tab_source_note(source_note = "This is a source note.") %>%
  tab_footnote(
    footnote = "This is a footnote.",
    locations = cells_body(columns = 1, rows = 1)
  ) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "The Title of the Table",
    subtitle = "The table's subtitle"
  ) %>%
  tab_stubhead(label = "Top Left")

tab_1

# Table striping is now an add-on
(tab_2 <- tab_1 %>% opt_add_row_striping())

# Using allcaps for labels is common use case for distinguishability
(tab_3 <- tab_2 %>% opt_all_caps())

# Sometimes the additional ink of top/bottom borders may not be desired
(tab_4 <- tab_3 %>% opt_remove_top_bottom_borders())

# The horizontal alignment of the table header can be easily
# modified with `opt_align_table_header()`
(tab_5 <- tab_4 %>% opt_align_table_header("left"))

# There are two options for table lining (one maximal, one minimal)
tab_1 %>% opt_fully_lined()
tab_1 %>% opt_lineless()
```

title: Fix row label display issue with `summary_rows()`
description: The row label wouldn't appear in a very wide table. Added tests to ensure that they are visible in both narrow and wide tables. Using the following example now produces the row labels for all summary rows (groupwise and grand summary rows): ```r library(gt) library(tidyverse) tbl <- dplyr::tibble( groups = c(rep("one", 5), rep("two", 5)), rows = 1:10 %>% as.character(), a = 1:10, b = 11:20, c = 21:30, d = 31:40, e = 41:50, f = 51:60, g = 61:70, h = 71:80, i = 81:90, j = 91:100, k = 101:110, l = 111:120, m = 121:130, n = 131:140, o = 141:150, p = 151:160, q = 161:170, r = 171:180, s = 181:190, t = 191:200 ) tbl %>% select(c("groups", "rows", letters[1:(ncol(tbl) - 2)])) %>% gt(rowname_col = "rows", groupname_col = "groups") %>% summary_rows( groups = "one", columns = letters[1:(ncol(tbl) - 2)], fns = list( the_sum = ~sum(.), mean = ~mean(.) ) ) %>% grand_summary_rows( columns = letters[1:(ncol(tbl) - 2)], fns = list( the_sum = ~sum(.), mean = ~mean(.) ) ) %>% tab_header(title = "The Table Title", subtitle = "The Table Subtitle") %>% tab_style( style = cell_text(align = "left"), locations = cells_title(groups = "title") ) %>% tab_style( style = cell_text(align = "left"), locations = cells_title(groups = "subtitle") ) ``` Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/353.

title: Rework color generation to favor rgba values when `alpha < 1`
description:
This PR modifies some of the utility functions that normalize colors and choose foreground text colors (for maximal contrast w.r.t. the background color). The change was made to effectively remove the use of `rrggbbaa` hex color values (which aren't compatible with older browsers, including the webkit implementation used in **webshot**) and either use `rrggbb` hex color values or rgba values when alpha is anything other than 1.

Here are some working examples of `gtsave()` with this change (previously, most background colors and cell striping wouldn't appear).

To solve this, it's proposed that the **webshot2** package instead be used. With this minimal change in place, the resulting PNG screenshot looks as it should. Before and after images are provided here.

A potential issue is that **webshot2** isn't on CRAN. This is okay so long as **gt** isn't submitted to CRAN before **webshot2** is. As with **webshot** before, **webshot2** is in Suggests.

title: Add vertical align option in `cell_text()`
description: This allows for selected cells to have their contents vertically aligned (`top`, `center`, and `bottom`). Currently, the vertical alignment of all cell content is `center`; there's no easy way to change this. This option is useful for tables with large chunks of text, where the less verbose columns end up way down the page. Here is an example where the option is used effectively: ```r library(gt) library(stringi) long_text <- stri_rand_lipsum(3) %>% str_c(., collapse = "\n") data.frame( index = c("I want this", "at the top", "of each cell"), text = long_text ) %>% gt() %>% tab_style( style = cell_text(v_align = "top"), locations = cells_data() ) ``` All CI tests pass with this fairly minimal change. Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/380

title: Fix several issues related to styling of an HTML table
description: This will fix a few issues mainly related to table options (accessed through the `tab_options()`): #337 and #361. Issue #337 is concerned with font sizing of the column labels. The overall table font size is `16px` and textual elements in most table locations have font sizes defined as percentages relative to the table font size. This is not the case for the column labels and for the row group labels. The change here is to make relative sizing consistent as a default. In this way, changing the `table_font_size` value will change font-size values for all text in the table (we can always explicitly provide a font-size in `px` for any of the text elements as well through `tab_options()`). All of this will make it possible to package up a set of options for predetermined table sizes (e.g., `small`, `medium`, `large`) in a future change. Other changes: - added new options in `tab_options()` for vertical lines and to access options for all extant horizontal lines - made consistent options in `tab_options` to be able to set a background color for each formal table location - added text manipulation options (e.g., font-size, text-transform) for certain table locations - the naming of the options within `tab_options()` is much more internally consistent - roxygen doc `@param`s have been reorganized/rewritten - minor corrections throughout package to use the refined argument names - corrected existing tests and added a plethora of new tests Future changes: With these changes, we finally have the ability to supply `preset_*()` functions that provide a distinct table look (and work on https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/238 can finally start). Here are a few example screenshots with the base table and some presets (one that removes all lines from the table, another that produces a fully lined table one, and, one that colors the locations differently): Given that there are a lot of options available in `tab_options()` (and I think this is justified), some thought should be given to helper functions to divide/define the options into those by location or parameter (two TODOs added to function body). There should also be an expansion of the `opt_*()` family of macro-type functions (e.g., `opt_footnote_marks()` makes it easy to define footnote marks without using `tab_options()`). Some ideas here are `opt_striping()`, `opt_table_outline()`, `opt_table_size()`, etc. Fixes #337 Fixes #361

title: CSS modifications
description: These changes improve (to my eyes, at least) to default appearance of an HTML table. Thin horizontal lines are used for each data row. All thicker lines has their colors lightened (from `#A8A8A8` to `#D3D3D3`) except for the top and bottom table lines. The default text is lightened from `#000000` to `#333333` (gray20). This is only slightly noticeable but it has the effect of softening the text somewhat. Padding in the table columns has been reduced and padding between the table Title and Subtitle has been tweaked for better optical positioning. Here are three examples with the new CSS changes.

title: Enable option to set row group padding in `tab_options()`
description: This PR allows us to use the `row_group.padding` option in `tab_options()` to specify a common padding value for row groups in a **gt** table (instead of the `8px` default). Here is an example: ```r exibble %>% gt(rowname_col = "row", groupname_col = "group") %>% tab_options(row_group.padding = px(24)) ``` Fixes: https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/327.

title: Fix for `cells_stub()` stylizing helper function
description: This is a simple fix to a `filter()` statement within `create_body_component_h()` that restores the ability to style stub cells. Here's a sample table after the fix is applied: ```r sza %>% dplyr::filter( latitude == 20 & tst <= "1000") %>% dplyr::select(-latitude) %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(sza)) %>% tidyr::spread(key = "tst", value = sza) %>% gt(rowname_col = "month") %>% fmt_missing( columns = TRUE, missing_text = "" ) %>% tab_style( style = list( cell_fill(color = "darkblue"), cell_text(color = "white") ), locations = cells_stub(rows = TRUE) ) %>% tab_style( style = list( cell_fill(color = "lightblue"), cell_text(color = "black") ), locations = cells_data(rows = TRUE) ) ``` Fixes: https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/339.

title: Incorporate alpha option to `cell_fill()`
description: This PR adds the `alpha` argument to the `cell_fill()` stylizing helper function. This also fixes the `data_color()` function, which had an `alpha` argument that wasn't implemented. Here are two examples that now work: ```r sza %>% dplyr::filter( latitude == 20 & tst <= "1000") %>% dplyr::select(-latitude) %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(sza)) %>% tidyr::spread(key = "tst", value = sza) %>% gt(rowname_col = "month") %>% fmt_missing( columns = TRUE, missing_text = "" ) %>% tab_style( style = list( cell_fill(color = "darkblue", alpha = 0.4), cell_text(color = "white") ), locations = list( cells_data(columns = everything()), cells_column_labels(columns = everything()) ) ) ``` ```r countrypops %>% dplyr::filter(country_name == "Mongolia") %>% dplyr::select(-contains("code")) %>% tail(10) %>% gt() %>% tab_options(row.striping.include_table_body = FALSE) %>% data_color( columns = vars(population), colors = c("red", "orange", "green", "blue"), alpha = 0.5 ) ``` Fixes: https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/250.

title: Fixes to `groups` arg of `cells_column_labels()`
description:
This PR incorporates resolver functions in the `cells_column_labels()` function as it pertains to `groups` (column spanner labels). The `resolve_cells_column_spanners()` util function allows inputs to be character vectors, spanner names in `vars()`, and select helpers like `starts_with()`.

This example now works:

```r
tibble(
  letter = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 3),
  id = rep(1:3, 2),
  x = runif(6),
  y = runif(6)
) %>% 
  gather(var, value, x:y) %>% 
  unite(column, letter, var) %>% 
  spread(column, value) %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_split_delim("_", everything()) %>%
  tab_footnote(
    footnote = "Source: the definitive guide to the alphabet",
    location = cells_column_labels(groups = everything())
  )
```

Fixes: https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/228.

title: Allow use of integers in `pct()`/`px()`
description:
Both the `pct()` and `px()` don't allow `integer`-class values as input (only `numeric`). This PR allows the use of integers, so, this will now work:

```r
sp500 %>%
  head() %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "S&P 500",
    subtitle = "5 rows"
  ) %>%
  tab_spanner(
    label = "prices",
    columns = vars(open, high, low, close)
  ) %>%
  fmt_date(
    columns = vars(date),
    date_style = 2
  ) %>%
  fmt_currency(
    columns = vars(open, high, low, close),
    currency = "USD"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = vars(volume),
    suffixing = TRUE
  ) %>%
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = px(10L)
  )
```

Fixes: https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/307.

title: Add function to specify column widths: `cols_widths()`
description: This PR allows for manual adjustments to column widths via the new `cols_widths()` function. We choose which columns get specific widths (in pixels, usually by use of the `px()` helper function) and all other columns are assigned a default width value though the `.others` argument. There are two ways make the width assignments, both occur in the `...`: (1) named arguments, where the names are those of the columns and the values are the dimensions (in `px` where, for instance, `px(80)` would helpfully generate `30px`), and, (2) paired `vars()`---`px()` expressions, which: - are separated by commas (e.g., `vars(col_b), px(120)`) - allow the use of one or more column names, column indices, or select helpers (e.g., `starts_with()`, `contains()`, `everything()`, etc.) within each `vars()` expression - cannot be mixed with named arguments as in (1) Here are two examples (using the two different expression styles) that make the same table: ```r # Use `exibble` to create a gt table; # with named arguments in `...`, we # can specify exact the widths for # those columns (the `.others` value # will provide a default width for # any unset columns) exibble %>% dplyr::select( num, char, date, datetime, row ) %>% gt() %>% cols_widths( num = px(150), char = px(100), date = px(200), datetime = px(200), .others = px(60) ) # We can take a different approach # in making the same table by using # paired `vars()`-dimension # expressions; these are all # unnamed and we need to ensure # alternation between `vars()` # and `px()` expressions exibble %>% dplyr::select( num, char, date, datetime, row ) %>% gt() %>% cols_widths( vars(num), px(150), vars(ends_with("r")), px(100), vars(starts_with("date")), px(200), .others = px(60) ) ``` Here is the table: Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/111.

title: Add the `path` argument to `gtsave()`
description:
The addition of a `path` argument to `gtsave()` aligns this function more closely to the `ggplot2::ggsave()` function. If a path is provided, then it will be combined with the `filename` argument. Path expansion still occurs (so the `~` can be safely used). Here is an example usage with the changes in this PR.

```r
library(gt)
library(tidyverse)

# Use `gtcars` to create a gt table; add
# a stubhead label to describe what is
# in the stub
tab_1 <-
  gtcars %>%
  dplyr::select(model, year, hp, trq) %>%
  dplyr::slice(1:5) %>%
  gt(rowname_col = "model") %>%
  tab_stubhead_label(label = "car")

# Save the HTML table as a PDF file; we
# can optionally add a separate `path`
tab_1 %>% gtsave("tab_1.pdf", path = "~")
```

This PR also improves the documentation for `gtsave()`, providing information on what options can be used in the `...` (with links to the underlying functions for more details).

Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/284.

title: Refactoring of the `tab_options()` function
description: This adds several utility functions that minimize repeated code for each options setting. The result is a single line setter (with internal preprocessing and assertion steps) for each option.

title: Make row group labels span the entire table (#128)
description:
I just tried out `gt` for the first time this week and found it very useful immediately, so thanks! I did run into issue #128 though, so I thought I would try a PR.

It produces the expected behaviour for the reprex in the original issue:

![latex_row_group_labels](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1460294/57451693-5bfd2d80-72a5-11e9-94b4-ed9fbd2a07c4.png)

title: Have the table ID be settable, random, or absent in `gt()`
description:
This change allows us to more explicitly set the table ID though the `id` option in `gt()`. By default this is set to use the new helper function `id_random()`, which is equivalent to the current behavior of having a 10-letter random string being generated with each `gt()` call. We can use a custom string here, or, use `NULL` to entirely disable ID generation. Here's a basic usage example where we set a custom `id` value: ```r library(gt) exibble %>% gt(id = "name") ``` The following screen capture shows that the `id` for the enclosing `
` is now set to `"name"`: Here's another showing that the `id` attr can be omitted entirely: ```r library(gt) exibble %>% gt(id = NULL) ``` Fixes: https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/141.

title: Add options related to the table <div>
description:
This PR adds the ability to modify the width and height of the enclosing table `
` for HTML output (though the `container.width` and `container.height` arguments in `tab_options()`). To make this work better with heights less than the actual table height, the `overflow-y` option has been set as `auto` to enable vertical scrolling (there is already the `overflow-x` option set for horizontal scrolling). This also adds the `table.align` argument (again, in `tab_options()`). It's now possible to `left`, `center` (default), and `right` align tables within the `
`. Here is an example: ```r library(gt) library(tidyverse) pizzaplace %>% dplyr::group_by(type, size) %>% dplyr::summarize( sold = n(), income = sum(price) ) %>% gt(rowname_col = "size") %>% tab_header(title = "Pizzas Sold in 2015") %>% fmt_number( columns = vars(sold), decimals = 0, use_seps = TRUE ) %>% fmt_currency( columns = vars(income), currency = "USD" ) %>% summary_rows( groups = TRUE, columns = vars(sold), fns = list(`Group Total` = "sum"), formatter = fmt_number, decimals = 0, use_seps = TRUE ) %>% summary_rows( groups = TRUE, columns = "income", fns = list(`Group Total` = "sum"), formatter = fmt_currency, currency = "USD" ) %>% grand_summary_rows( columns = "income", fns = list(`All Sales` = "sum"), formatter = fmt_currency, currency = "USD" ) %>% tab_options( summary_row.background.color = "#ACEACE", grand_summary_row.background.color = "steelblue", row_group.background.color = "#FFEFDB", table.width = pct(90), container.height = px(300), container.width = px(600), table.align = "right" ) ``` Here is the table in a browser with the Web Inspector showing the layout: Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/206. Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/168.

title: Allow an empty table with zero rows to create an empty gt table
description: If we use table data with 0 rows but some columns defined, we get an error (and it's not informative). Here's an example: ```r sp500 %>% head(0) %>% gt() ``` ``` Error in value[[jvseq[[jjj]]]] : subscript out of bounds ``` This PR considers that zero-row table to be valid input and so a rendered table with no rows will appear. Here is the output of the above statement with the changes here: Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/87.

title: Adding the `currency()` helper function for specifying custom currencies
description: This PR adds the `currency()` helper function, which makes it easy to specify a context-aware currency symbol to `currency` argument of `fmt_currency()`. Because **gt** can render tables to several output formats, `currency()` allows for different variations of the custom symbol based on the output context (which are `html`, `latex`, and `default`). One condition is that we specify a value for the `decimals` argument in the `fmt_currency()` call (unless the option `use_subunits` is set to `FALSE`). Here is an example where we can specify context-aware currency strings, where the output table is HTML. ```r library(gt) sp500 %>% head() %>% gt() %>% fmt_currency( columns = vars(open), currency = currency( html = "₿", latex = "BTC", default = "btc"), decimals = 2 ) ``` If this were a LaTeX table, we would see values such as `BTC2,060.59`. Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/243.

title: Path expand all file inputs
description:
This addresses https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/277, where file paths with `~`s aren't expanded. This also fixes other instances by normalizing file paths with `fs::path_expand()`.

Fixes: https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/277.

title: Add the `cells_stubhead_label()` location helper
description: This adds the location helper function `cells_stubhead_label()`, and this makes it possible to add a footnote and styles to this single location. Here is an example of how this works: ```r library(gt) sza %>% dplyr::filter( latitude == 20 & month == "jan" & !is.na(sza) ) %>% dplyr::select(-latitude, -month) %>% gt(rowname_col = "tst") %>% tab_header(title = "Solar Zenith Angles") %>% tab_stubhead_label(label = "tst") %>% tab_footnote( footnote = "Number indicates height of sun.", locations = cells_column_labels( columns = vars(sza)) ) %>% tab_footnote( footnote = "True Solar Time.", locations = cells_stubhead_label() ) %>% tab_style( style = cell_fill(color = "lightgreen"), locations = cells_stubhead_label() ) %>% tab_style( style = cell_text(color = "purple"), locations = cells_stubhead_label() ) %>% tab_footnote( footnote = "Uses the `sza` dataset.", locations = cells_title(groups = "title") ) ``` This is part of an effort to make all possible locations accessible for footnotes and styles (at this time, groupwise and grand summary captions in the stub still do not have location helpers). We eventually want to have all possible location helpers available to create a `cells_all()` location helper as recommended in https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/176. Fixes: https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/224

title: Store empty-string value in `sep` vector

title: [WIP] Add the `cell_borders()` helper and update implementation of the stylizing helper fcns
description: This adds the `cell_borders()` helper function for selectively modifying cell borders in a `tab_style()` call. The existing `cells_styles()` helper was reworked as `cell_text()` and the single argument dealing with the cell background color was put in `cell_fill()`. These three stylizing helper functions can be placed in a `list()` of calls for the `style` argument of `tab_style()`, allowing us to target cells and perform multiple stylizing operations on the targets at once. Here is an example: ```r library(gt) exibble %>% gt() %>% tab_style( style = list( cell_borders( selection = c("left", "right"), color = "green", style = "solid", weight = px(3) ), cell_fill(color = "lightgray"), cell_text(color = "steelblue", font = "HelveticaNeue") ), locations = cells_data(columns = vars(row, char)) ) ``` Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/258. Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/245. cc: https://github.com/ddsjoberg/gtsummary/issues/78

title: Use webshot to generate images of HTML tables
description:
With this PR, we can use the webshot package's `webshot()` function to generate image files based on the HTML table. The image files are cropped to the `table` element and contain some padding as well. This is handled through the `gtsave()` function with the `gt_save_webshot()` function used in the switch statement (which calls different output functions based on the output file's extension).

We check if the webshot package is installed with `requireNamespace()` and suggest that it should be installed if it isn't available.

The following statement

```r

exibble %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = md("The exibble dataset")
  ) %>%
  gtsave("ex.png")
```

Gives us this output:

![ex](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5612024/56084234-1fe9c080-5dfe-11e9-8110-41c3860f694d.png)

Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/256.
Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/96.

title: Move roxygen documentation to Markdown
description:
This PR makes a change in the way that roxygen documentation is prepared. It now moves to Markdown formatting, with the setting defined in the DESCRIPTION.

Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/246.

title: Escaping for row group label
description: This fixes an HTML rendering bug, where row group labels aren't escaped at render time. For example, the following code ```r library(gt) data.frame(age = c("0<=x<=30", "30% gt(groupname_col = "age") ``` gives us This is because the unescaped `<` results in the completion of the innerHTML. With the fix provided here, this example now works: Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/249.

title: Fix for Markdown/HTML-formatting of spanner column labels
description:
Using the `md()` or `html()` helper function to format spanner column labels became broken after function used to detect the `html` class was created and used (because it would fail to detect the `html` class, it would `htmlEscape()` the HTML text). This fixes the utility function (now renamed as `is_html()`) and adds several tests to ensure that the HTML is preserved and also that Markdown formatting for spanner column labels works. Here is an example, with the changes from the PR: ``` library(tidyverse) library(gt) airquality_m <- airquality %>% mutate(Year = 1973L) %>% slice(1:10) %>% select(Month, Day, Year) # Create a display table using the `airquality` # dataset; arrange columns into groups gt_tbl <- gt(data = airquality_m) %>% tab_header( title = "New York Air Quality Measurements", subtitle = "Daily measurements in New York City (May 1-10, 1973)" ) %>% tab_spanner( label = html("Time
n = 10"), columns = vars(Year, Month, Day) ) # Show the gt table gt_tbl ``` Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/247

title: Make several refactoring improvements to some `format_*()` functions
description: These changes provide a few more improvements to some `format_*()` functions and related utility functions.

title: Refactoring of heading component
description:
This builds upon the earlier refactoring effort, which made available several new utility functions for composing strings. Additional utility functions are included here to help with gathering footnote glyphs and custom styles for cells.

Templating with `glue` is used here to compose the HTML and LaTeX fragments (along with `paste_between()`). Some improvements to the CSS classes for the title and subtitle were also made.

title: Include option to hide all column labels
description: Sometimes it can be very useful not to have column labels at all. This PR makes that possible by providing the `column_labels.hide` argument in `tab_options()`. Here is a working example: ```r # Create a few Markdown-based # text snippets text_1a <- " ### This is Markdown. Markdown’s syntax is comprised entirely of punctuation characters, which punctuation characters have been carefully chosen so as to look like what they mean... assuming you’ve ever used email. " text_1b <- " Info on Markdown syntax can be found [here](https://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/). " text_1c <- "" text_2a <- " The **gt** package has these datasets: - `countrypops` - `sza` - `gtcars` - `sp500` - `pizzaplace` - `exibble` " text_2b <- " There's a quick reference [here](https://commonmark.org/help/). " text_2c <- " Yes, gifs should work. " # Arrange the text snippets as a tibble # using the `dplyr::tribble()` function; # then, create a gt table and format # all columns with `fmt_markdown()` dplyr::tribble( ~Markdown, ~md, text_1a, text_2a, text_1b, text_2b, text_1c, text_2c, ) %>% gt() %>% fmt_markdown(columns = TRUE) %>% tab_options( table.width = px(500), column_labels.hide = TRUE ) ``` Closes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/225.

title: Enable table striping options
description: There are settings in `tab_options()` that allow us to enable/disable row striping both in the table body and also in the stub. Unfortunately, these options didn't do anything. With this PR, they are now operational. Here are a few examples. First, here's the default case: ```r library(gt) library(tidyverse) exibble %>% select(num, currency, row, group) %>% gt(groupname_col = "group", rowname_col = "row") ``` Here is row striping both in the table body and also in the table stub: ```r exibble %>% select(num, currency, row, group) %>% gt(groupname_col = "group", rowname_col = "row") %>% tab_options( row.striping.include_table_body = TRUE, row.striping.include_stub = TRUE ) ``` One last example, where the stub has stripes and the table body does not: ```r exibble %>% select(num, currency, row, group) %>% gt(groupname_col = "group", rowname_col = "row") %>% tab_options( row.striping.include_table_body = FALSE, row.striping.include_stub = TRUE ) ``` This fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/199.

title: Refactoring of formatter functions
description:
The formatting functions (`format_*()`) need to be refactored to reduce code complexity and redundancy, and also to provide a means to better test smaller components.

This PR focuses on creating a comprehensive suite of helper functions for the various `format_*()` functions (some of which will also be helpful for other package internals), many more tests, and better structuring of the formatter functions. 

Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/229, and fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/235.

title: Fix for `fmt_date()` that allows `Date` columns to work
description:
Currently, the `fmt_date()` function only works with character-based columns with an ISO formatted date or date-time. This PR makes it possible to also use values of type `Date` (as in the `sp500` dataset). The example in the `README` sidesteps the problem by mutating a date column (with `Date`s) to a `character` column:

```r
sp500 %>%
  dplyr::filter(date >= start_date & date <= end_date) %>%
  dplyr::select(-adj_close) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(date = as.character(date)) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "S&P 500",
    subtitle = glue::glue("{start_date} to {end_date}")
  ) %>%
  fmt_date(
    columns = vars(date),
    date_style = 3
  ) %>%
  fmt_currency(
    columns = vars(open, high, low, close),
    currency = "USD"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = vars(volume),
    scale_by = 1 / 1E9,
    pattern = "{x}B"
  )
```
The PR makes this work without that `mutate()` call.

Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/202.

title: Avoid formatting of cells with NA values
description:
The reason for this change is to make is very easy to format values in one pass and handle missing values in another sweep—without explicitly specifying which cells have those missing values. To illustrate the problem and the benefits of the solution, let's use the `sza` dataset for its intended purpose: creating a table of solar zenith angles during sunrise for every month at a reference latitude. Here's the code: ```r library(gt) library(tidyverse) sza %>% dplyr::filter(latitude == 20) %>% dplyr::select(-latitude) %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(sza)) %>% tidyr::spread(key = "tst", value = sza) %>% gt(rowname_col = "month") %>% fmt_number( columns = TRUE, decimals = 1 ) %>% fmt_missing( columns = TRUE, missing_text = "" ) %>% cols_align( align = "center", columns = TRUE ) %>% tab_stubhead_label(label = html("month
(20°N)")) %>% tab_header(title = html("☀ Solar Zenith Angles ☀")) %>% tab_options( column_labels.font.size = "smaller", table.font.size = "smaller", row.padding = px(3) ) ``` Here is the gt table before the PR changes: And here is the better version with the changes of the PR in place: Before the PR, the second formatter would *win* and nullify the numeric formatting (notice that some numbers have no decimal values). Changing the order of the formatters would have all numbers being formatted to a single decimal place, but `NA` values would be present. The new way allows for any ordering of the two formatters because `fmt_missing()` won't interfere with cells operated on by the other formatters (which avoid processing `NA` cells). Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/79.

title: Add the `fmt_markdown()` function
description: This adds the formatter function, `fmt_markdown()`, that transforms Markdown-formatted text into the correct output format. Here is an example of its use: ```r first <- "Here is a **list** of numbers: - one - two - three " second <- "Here is line *one*, and this is line *two*." tibble(markdown_text = c(first, second)) %>% gt() %>% fmt_markdown(columns = vars(markdown_text)) ``` Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/190.

title: Fix for `cells_group()` and it's use in `tab_style()`
description: This PR addresses a bug where custom styles cannot be applied to stub row labels through `tab_style()` and `cells_group()`. For example, with ```r exibble %>% gt(rowname_col = "row", groupname_col = "group") %>% tab_style( locations = cells_group(groups = "grp_a"), style = cells_styles(text_align = "center", bkgd_color = "lightblue") ) ``` we would get the error: ``` Error in arrange_impl(.data, dots) : Evaluation error: object 'colnum' not found. ``` With the changes proposed here, we now get to style row group label cells. ```r exibble %>% gt(rowname_col = "row", groupname_col = "group") %>% tab_style( locations = cells_group(groups = "grp_a"), style = cells_styles(text_align = "center", bkgd_color = "lightblue") ) ``` A testthat test was added to verify that custom styles could now be applied to this location. Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/182.

title: Bugfixes and improvements to `summary_rows()`
description: This addresses a bug (https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/142) where aggregation function would operate on all columns and retain only the results for the requested columns. The prior behavior easily results in failures when an aggregation function operates on any column with incompatible data. The PR also adds functionality for grand summaries (https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/38, https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/68). If `groups == FALSE` we obtain a collection of summary rows that operate on all of the data in the table. We can have both groupwise summaries and grand summaries in the same output table. Grand summaries are distinguishable from groupwise summaries by use of a large double border (and placement at the bottom of the table) Finally, the PR applies several fixes for summary label generation and catches several edge cases. It's both more flexible, less prone to failure, and stops (with nice messages) if some of the stricter rules aren't followed. The documentation has been updated to reflect these changes. Here's a table using a groupwise summary (across all groups): ```r sp500 %>% dplyr::filter( date >= "2015-01-05" & date <="2015-01-16" ) %>% dplyr::arrange(date) %>% dplyr::mutate( week = paste0( "W", strftime(date, format = "%V")) ) %>% dplyr::select(-adj_close, -volume) %>% gt( rowname_col = "date", groupname_col = "week" ) %>% summary_rows( groups = TRUE, columns = vars(open, high, low, close), fns = list( min = ~min(.), max = ~max(.), avg = ~mean(.)), formatter = fmt_number, use_seps = FALSE ) ``` Here's a table using a grand summary: ```r sp500 %>% dplyr::filter( date >= "2015-01-05" & date <="2015-01-16" ) %>% dplyr::arrange(date) %>% dplyr::mutate( week = paste0( "W", strftime(date, format = "%V")) ) %>% dplyr::select(-adj_close, -volume) %>% gt( rowname_col = "date", groupname_col = "week" ) %>% summary_rows( groups = FALSE, columns = vars(open, high, low, close), fns = list( min = ~min(.), max = ~max(.), avg = ~mean(.)), formatter = fmt_number, use_seps = FALSE ) ``` Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/38 Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/68 Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/142

title: Fix for `fmt_scientific()` when using very large or small numbers
description:
This fix modifies the `is_equal_to()` util function, which now uses an `identical()` comparison (instead of `all.equal()`) between two numbers. This has important implications for the `fmt_scientific()` formatter function because we compare whether a number is equal to zero and apply scientific notation when a number isn't zero (among other conditions not mentioned here).

Very small numbers would erroneously be deemed equal to zero before this change, resulting in incorrect formatting of such numbers in scientific notation.

Now, if we apply scientific notation to these numbers

`-1.5E200`, `-1.5E100`, `-2.5E0`, `-3.5E-100`, `-3.5E-200`, `1.5E-200`, `1.5E-100`, `2.5E0`, `3.5E100`, `3.5E200`

we get (in the default context)

`-1.50000 x 10(200)`, `-1.50000 x 10(100)`, `-2.50000`, `-3.50000 x 10(-100)`, `-3.50000 x 10(-200)`, `1.50000 x 10(-200)`, `1.50000 x 10(-100)`, `2.50000`, `3.50000 x 10(100)`, `3.50000 x 10(200)`

Tests have been added to ensure that very large or small numbers are formatted correctly in scientific notation.

title: Improvements to resolving column indices and names
description:
Here we split out `resolve_vars()` -> `resolve_vars()` (returns column names) & `resolve_vars_idx()` (returns column indices).

The `resolve_vars_idx()` now takes the place of the earlier `resolve_vars()` and the new `resolve_vars()` wraps `resolve_vars_idx()` and uses `data` (a variable that's available in almost every API function) to translate the column indices to column names.

This standardizes the means to resolve to column names and indices when the user provides column names in various ways.

Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/53

To limit the size of the displayed table somewhat, there is a `begins_with` argument (which is also in the `info_currencies()` function) that filters by the first letter in the base locale ID. title: Allow for easy insertion of ggplot plots in a table column via a formatter
description: The new `fmt_ggplot()` function allows for easier inclusion of **ggplot2** plots (within a list column of the input table data) into a **gt** table. The common pattern toward obtaining these plots is through mutation of a list column containing all the `data` required for plot: ```r %>% dplyr::group_by() %>% tidyr::nest(.key = plot) %>% dplyr::mutate(plot = purrr::map(plot, )) ``` While the PR contains functionality to detect and automatically format columns containing **ggplot2** plots, we can also opt to use the `fmt_ggplot()` function to allow us to specify `rows` and set options for the plots' `height` and `aspect_ratio`. Here are some examples of how this would work: ```r # Create a small table with a `plot` column gtcars_plot_column <- gtcars %>% dplyr::group_by(mfr) %>% tidyr::nest(.key = plot) %>% dplyr::mutate( plot = map(plot, ~ggplot(., aes(hp, trq)) + geom_point())) %>% head(3) # Automatic formatting of plots in `plot` using # default options tab_1 <- gtcars_plot_column %>% gt() # Using `fmt_ggplot()` to provide values # for `columns`, `height` and `aspect_ratio` tab_2 <- gtcars_plot_column %>% gt() %>% fmt_ggplot( columns = vars(plot), height = 200, aspect_ratio = 2.5 ) ``` Here are images of `tab_1` and `tab_2`: These are minimal examples showing the basic usage of inserting plots, so, the resulting tables look less than ideal. With some extra care given to setting common axis ranges and using `ggplot2::theme()` to increase font sizes, line widths, etc., inserted plots would become more aesthetically pleasing. Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/152

title: Add option to gather columns in `tab_spanner()`
description: Currently, `tab_spanner()` will not move columns to create a contiguous block of columns under a spanner heading. While this is acceptable when you want a repeating spanner column label across the top of the column labels, it's likely not the most common use case. This change adds a `gather` argument that's set to `TRUE`. This makes it convenient for automatically gathering the columns that are part of a single spanner column label. Before the change, the user would have to carefully ensure the columns are contiguous before entry in `gt()`, or, would need to use some of the `cols_move*()` functions for manual movement of columns. Here is an example where columns are automatically moved under the spanner column label ```r gtcars %>% dplyr::select( -mfr, -trim, bdy_style, drivetrain, -drivetrain, -trsmn, -ctry_origin ) %>% dplyr::slice(1:8) %>% gt(rowname_col = "model") %>% tab_header(title = "gtcars") %>% tab_spanner( label = "performance", columns = vars( hp, hp_rpm, trq, trq_rpm, mpg_c, mpg_h) ) %>% tab_spanner( label = "model info", columns = vars( bdy_style, year, msrp) ) ``` and this yields the following **gt** output table: The key thing to note here is that the `msrp` column in the second `tab_spanner()` call is separated from the `bdy_style` and `year` set of columns. The function now recognizes these gaps and moves columns together whilst preserving the ordering of columns in the group. Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/110. Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/127. Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/102.

title: Add support for large-number suffixing
description: This change makes it possible to apply automatic scaling and suffixing (with a predefined or custom symbol set) to larger numbers—thousands, millions, billions, trillions. A single argument `suffixing` provides the interface for this transformation in `fmt_number()` and `fmt_currency()`. The argument accepts a `TRUE` or `FALSE` (the default), whereby `TRUE` performs the autoscaling/suffixing with a default set of symbols. The `suffixing` argument could also accept a 4-element character vector understood to represent replacement symbols for the stock `K`, `M`, `B`, and `T` (`NA` values can be used here to exclude those particular ranges from taking part in the transformation). By way of example, we can use `countrypops` to build a **gt** table and format all of the columns with `fmt_number()` whilst using `suffixing = TRUE` ```r countrypops %>% dplyr::select( country_code_3, year, population) %>% dplyr::filter( country_code_3 %in% c( "CHN", "IND", "USA", "PAK", "IDN") ) %>% dplyr::filter(year > 1975 & year %% 5 == 0) %>% tidyr::spread(year, population) %>% dplyr::arrange(desc(`2015`)) %>% gt(rowname_col = "country_code_3") %>% fmt_number( columns = TRUE, decimals = 2, suffixing = TRUE ) ``` and this yields the following output table: The alternative before the change is to use a very large number of `fmt_number()` statements that each use conditional statements to target cells within fixed ranges before applying numerical scaling and pattern-based formatting to each. Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/134

title: Add function to get LaTeX dependencies for external use
description:
An exported function is added here (`get_latex_dependencies()`) to make it easier to declare which packages are required for **gt** when using Rnw. A minimal example:

````
%!sweave=knitr

\documentclass{article}

<<results='asis', echo=FALSE>>=
gt::get_latex_dependencies()
@

\begin{document}

Content...

\end{document}
````  

Using the `get_latex_dependencies()` function in this way places the LaTeX `\use_package{}` statements before the document start, which is convenient when using a **gt** table within the document. This change also centralizes the names of the LaTeX packages that are used in the LaTeX-rendering pipeline and in the aforementioned function.

title: Fixes to restore RTF output support
description:
These small changes (essentially just creating two local variables and modifying a few function calls) restore RTF support. Now, any table created in an R Markdown document with the `rtf_document` output format will be properly integrated into the .rtf file (also, as before, the entire document opens in Word and the **gt** table is included). Here is an example .Rmd file:

````
---
output: rtf_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(gt)
```

# gt Table in RTF document

```{r}
gtcars %>%
  dplyr::filter(ctry_origin == "Germany") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(mfr) %>%
  dplyr::top_n(2, msrp) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(mfr, model, drivetrain, msrp) %>%
  gt()
```
````

Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/98.

title: Fix for footnote ordering in column spanner labels and column labels
description: Footnotes should always be put in the correct order (left-to-right then top-to-bottom). However, for footnote glyphs in the column labels, there was no strict ordering (i.e., left to chance by the API order). This example ```r gtcars %>% dplyr::filter(ctry_origin == "Germany") %>% dplyr::group_by(mfr) %>% dplyr::top_n(2, msrp) %>% dplyr::ungroup() %>% dplyr::select(mfr, model, drivetrain, msrp) %>% gt() %>% tab_footnote( footnote = "Prices in USD.", locations = cells_column_labels(columns = vars(msrp)) ) %>% tab_footnote( footnote = "AWD = All Wheel Drive, RWD = Rear Wheel Drive.", locations = cells_column_labels(columns = vars(drivetrain)) ) ``` would produce the following HTML output table (which has an incorrect ordering of footnotes): With the fixes in this PR, we now get the correct ordering. There was also a similar issue with column spanner labels and this PR applies the right ordering to that as well. This more comprehensive example ```r gtcars %>% dplyr::filter(ctry_origin == "Germany") %>% dplyr::group_by(mfr) %>% dplyr::top_n(2, msrp) %>% dplyr::ungroup() %>% dplyr::select(mfr, model, drivetrain, msrp) %>% gt() %>% tab_footnote( footnote = "Prices in USD.", locations = cells_column_labels(columns = vars(msrp)) ) %>% tab_footnote( footnote = "AWD = All Wheel Drive, RWD = Rear Wheel Drive.", locations = cells_column_labels(columns = vars(drivetrain)) ) %>% tab_footnote( footnote = "The most important details.", locations = cells_column_labels(groups = "specs and pricing") ) %>% tab_footnote( footnote = "German cars only.", locations = cells_column_labels(groups = "make and model") ) %>% tab_spanner(label = "make and model", columns = vars(mfr, model)) %>% tab_spanner(label = "specs and pricing", columns = vars(drivetrain, msrp)) ``` Produces a table with the correct footnote ordering, no matter the order of the `tab_footnote()` calls: Tests were added to check for the correct footnote ordering using the 2nd example above. Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/101.

title: Title/subtitle fix for inlining with existing custom styles
description: When a table has a custom style applied to either the title or the subtitle (through `tab_style()`), and, the table is exported to an HTML with inlined CSS styles, the title or subtitle won't span across the width of the table. The following code will produce a correct table in the Viewer: ```r gt(mtcars[1:2, ]) %>% tab_header( title = "The title", subtitle = "The subtitle" ) %>% tab_style( cells_styles( text_align = "left"), locations = list( cells_title(groups = "title"), cells_title(groups = "subtitle") ) ) ``` When it is exported to HTML via `as_raw_html()` and saved to disk, the viewed HTML won't have the `colspan` attr in the title or in the subtitle. This PR fixes that erroneous result by preserving the `colspan` attr. A testthat test has also been added. Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/113

title: Add PDF and raster image exporting functions
description:
By interfacing with the `wkhtmltopdf` and `wkhtmltoimage` binaries (pre-compiled, all platforms, and easy-to-install) we can create PDF and raster image files that are replicas of what is visible in the RStudio Viewer.

Here is the example usage for a PNG file:

```r
# Use `countrypops` to create a gt table;
# export the table as a PNG file
countrypops %>%
  dplyr::select(-contains("code")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(country_name == "Mongolia") %>%
  tail(5) %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = vars(population)
  ) %>%
  gt_png(file_name = "countrypops.png")
```

The output file looks like this:

![countrypops](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5612024/49883148-1163ac00-fe00-11e8-81ca-a9aa1ab3b411.png)

where the image whitespace on the left and right is trimmed by default (this is an option). 

Addresses #96 and partially solves the issue in https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/97.

title: Improvement to the handling of a `pattern` in most `fmt*()` functions
description:
This adds a utility function to replace multiple instances of `{x}` in the vector of formatted character values. This requires https://github.com/rstudio/gt/pull/94 to be merged first, then the `fmt_scientific()` function will be modified with this change.

All current tests pass with the change. More tests should be added to verify that the additional functionality works.

This fixes #61.

title: Fix for using of `fmt_scientific()` on columns with NA values
description: Previously, this code... ```r dplyr::tibble(x = c(-15.0, -1.5, -0.001, NA, 0, 0.001, 1.5, 22.5, 333.5)) %>% gt() %>% fmt_scientific(columns = vars(x)) ``` ...would result in this error: ``` Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) : subscript out of bounds ``` The error occurred because there was no treatment of `NA`s as with the other `fmt*()` functions. With the changes here, we don't get an error and gt table output is correct: A test was added to check the `fmt_scientific()` function for resilience to `NA` values. This fixes #80.

title: Modify options set in `format()`
description: Some options to `format()` in the `migrate_unformatted_to_output()` were left with default values (the `trim` and `justify` args), and this results in character values with some padding based on the longest values. While great for console printing, it results in inconsistent formatting in tables. Here is an example *before* and *after* the change with the following code: ```r dplyr::tibble(idx = 1:10, values = 501:510) %>% gt() %>% cols_merge( col_1 = vars(values), col_2 = vars(idx), pattern = "{1} ({2})" ) ``` *before* *after*

title: Removal of word "boxhead" (e.g., function names, documentation, tests, etc.)
description:
This is a careful renaming exercise where the word "boxhead" is replaced by "columns". This is a comprehensive replacement meant to simplify the terminology used within the API. It was started with 
issue https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/81 and PR https://github.com/rstudio/gt/pull/82 and this PR continues this work (and fixes #90).

All tests pass with these changes (manual and testthat).

title: Add default value for `currency` in `fmt_currency()`
description:
This adds a default currency of `"USD"` for the `currency` argument. Internal documentation for the `currency` parameter is updated, and, one testthat test was added to `test-fmt_currency.R`.  

Fixes #88

title: [WIP] Changes to `render_formats()` and improved NA-handling for formatters
description: This is an important infrastructural change that @schloerke kindly initiated during a meeting. It simplifies the rendering pipeline for the internal `data_df`, and makes `data_df` a list column `data.frame` during formatting. All of the `fmt_*()` functions have been modified to operate on list columns and better handle `NA`s and negative values (for the optional negative value text transformations). The `fmt_missing()` function has been renamed to `fmt_na()`. And all relevant `fmt_*()` functions now have an `na_value` argument where if a value is supplied, `fmt_na()` will be called internally on the `data` first. This allows for formatting and NA-handling with a single function call. Also, this fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/79. So even if we use a formatter function and then `fmt_na()` on the same cells (or the reverse), we get the preferred behavior of `NA` handling occurring for the `NA` cells and cell formatting on the other cells. ```r exibble %>% gt( rowname_col = "row", groupname_col = "group" ) %>% fmt_na( columns = vars(num), value = "missing" ) %>% fmt_number( columns = vars(num), decimals = 4 ) ``` In the `num` column, we can now successfully format the column to 4 decimal places with `fmt_number()` and process missing values with `fmt_na()`. Previously, one function would override the other (with a non-ideal workaround of having to specify the exact rows for each formatter function to obtain the result shown here). All tests and documentation have been modified, as has vignettes, etc. Tests and R CMD Check pass on dev and Travis. All manual tests with the .R/.Rmd scripts work as well.

title: API refinements for better clarity
description:
These changes are entirely name changes for several functions (and one or two arguments). It's intended to clarify the terminology used throughout the API. All changes were carefully made to the functions, examples, roxygen docs, tests, and example .R/.Rmd files. 

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/81.

title: Fix for inlining CSS styles in raw HTML output
description:
This provides a reasonable fix for the CSS-style inlining utility functions. The issue was that inlining would always create a new `style` attribute even if there were an existing `style` attribute (added in by use of `tab_style()`). The commits in this PR take into account any existing `style` attribute and merges in CSS rules derived from classes.

Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/36.

title: Add the `exibble` tibble as a dataset
description: Adds a toy dataset that is small but contains columns and data well-suited for easy experimentation with **gt**'s API without producing unwieldy output. With this, we can test out formatters, easily create a stub and row groups, and see how `NA` values work inside **gt**.

title: Update vignettes
description:
This updates existing vignettes and adds new vignettes.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/44.

title: Improvements to the `apply_styles()` function
description: This adds new properties for CSS fonts.

title: Add AppVeyor CI builds for Windows testing
description:
This complements the Linux and macOS testing with Travis CI. This might be non-functional until the repo becomes public. Otherwise we'd have to following these (possibly dangerous) recommendations: https://help.appveyor.com/discussions/problems/1853-how-to-add-a-private-project.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/72.

title: New datasets for the package
description:
This adds new datasets to the package so that we demonstrate how different **gt** features might be applied to different types of data. So far, it's a work in progress and 4–5 different datasets would be sufficient. These will be used in vignettes and in many other places.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/67

title: Allow Latex tables to break across PDF pages
description:
This adds in the `longtable` LaTeX package and modifies the construction of LaTeX so that it is `longtable` compatible. Now, tables break across pages without any user intervention.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/69

title: Latex `fmt_percent()` fix
description:
This provides a fix for `fmt_percent()` where the percentage sign wasn't being escaped for the Latex output mode. Latex-specific **testthat** tests are also changed to account for this correction.

Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/64.

title: Add `latex_dependency()` packages
description:
This removes the need for the user to declare the Latex packages `booktabs` and `caption` when rendering Latex tables. 

Within the `as_latex()` function (the 2nd pipeline step after the common part) the Latex table is generated and `knitr::asis_output()` is called on it. The `meta` argument is now used in that function, accepting a list of `rmarkdown::latex_dependency()` calls (with `booktabs` and `caption`).

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/63.

title: Add several versions of R as Travis jobs
description:
This adds several versions of R (going back to 3.2) as well as `devel`.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/59.

title: Latex testthat tests
description:
As most of the tests are currently focused on the `gt_tbl` object and the resultant HTML output, this PR is concerned with tests specifically for the Latex output code.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/56.

title: Table width and table stub style changes
description: These changes improve the appearance of the table when rendered to HTML. The table should is now centered in the content area and won't (by default) take 100% of the width. Also, the row captions in the stub area are now left-aligned and have a slight indent (to visually separate the row captions from the stub group captions). Here is a screenshot of the table as it now appears in Chrome. Some tests have been changed to take account of these changes. Closes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/54.

title: Modify storage and processing of column labels
description:
These changes delay the processing of column label text until the rendering pipeline of `build_data()`. Any markdown-formatted text is resolved correctly in both the HTML and Latex contexts. The `cols_label()` and `cols_split_delim()` functions have been rewritten to interact with a list of column names/labels. Tests have been modified to account for these changes and all of them pass.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/51.

title: Make changes to the processing of output text
description: This modifies the handling of input text (e.g., titles, source notes, etc.) by preserving their text-formatting classes and only processing the text during the render pipeline. This also addresses a **tidyeval** issue with conditional inputs for `rows` in all of the `fmt_*()` functions.

title: Add functions for coloring cell data
description: This adds two exported functions for coloring the background of data cells: `bg_color_fill_manual()` and `bg_color_gradient_n()`.

title: Refactor code that contains loops
description:
Some loops are converted to various `*apply` statements, or, avoid the use of a numeric index where possible. Goal is to vectorize wherever possible and get small speed gains.

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/40.

title: Remove requirement to use `funs()` when adding aggregation functions for a summary
description:
Removes the requirement to contain aggregation functions for `summary_rows()` with `dplyr::funs()`. Instead, a simple list is expected. Most methods of passing functions work the same as before except that the function calls (not bare names, though) require the use of the R formula interface (with `~`). 

This fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/18 and the issue itself arose from discussion at https://github.com/tidyverse/dplyr/issues/3094 and some personal communication.

Tests and examples have been changed to reflect the new usage.

Previous Usage:

```
gt(tbl) %>%
  summary_rows(
    groups = c("A", "C"),
    columns = vars(value_1),
    funs = funs(
      average = mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
      total = sum(., na.rm = TRUE),
      `std dev` = sd(., na.rm = TRUE)))
```

Proposed Usage:

```
gt(tbl) %>%
  summary_rows(
    groups = c("A", "C"),
    columns = vars(value_1),
    fns = list(
      average = ~mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
      total = ~sum(., na.rm = TRUE),
      `std dev` = ~sd(., na.rm = TRUE)))
```

title: Latex rendering support
description:
Added functions to enable Latex output support. A Latex table is returned using the `as_latex()` function. In an R Markdown context (where the output format is `pdf_document`) this creates a Latex table within a PDF document, otherwise a single-length vector with the Latex table lines is provided (can be written to file with `writeLines()`).

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/34.

title: RTF rendering support
description:
Added/updated functions that restore RTF output support. RTF is returned using the `as_rtf()` function. In an R Markdown context (where the output format is `rtf_document`) this creates an RTF table, otherwise a single-length vector with the RTF lines is provided (can be written to file with `writeLines()`).

Updates include enhancements to display footnote glyphs correctly and to style table text so that it looks reasonable in MS Word. 

Closes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/33.

title: Add several testthat test files
description: This adds 6 testthat .R files that test a variety of functions. When merged to master, this will bring code coverage up to ~73%.

title: Implement a simpler `cols_label()` function
description: This greatly simplifies the `cols_label()` function. It now takes in a set of named arguments in `...` and we can still use the helper functions `md()` and `html()` for formatting. Fixes https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/19.

title: Format non-`fmt()`ed data with `format()`
description: Also handles list columns with comma-separated, unquoted formatting. Fixes#16.

title: Fixes for `cols_align*()` functions
description: This provides fixes for a bug where a hidden column (via `cols_hide()`) would be unhidden from later use of any `cols_align*()` function. This also cleans up the `cols_align()` function. Tests are included here.

title: Fix for sass package renaming (and function changes)
description: This provides fixes for the recent renaming of `sassr` to `sass`. The `sass()` function is now used (since `compile_sass()` is now gone).

title: Add testthat tests for a range of utility/helper functions and for `gt_preview()`
description: This adds 5 testthat files to the **gt** test suite.

title: Fix for `gt_preview()` function's ellipsis row
description: Fixes visible rowname for ellipsis row. Also, better handling for situation where an ellipsis row is not required (i.e., there are fewer table rows than head + tail rows requested).

title: Remove `data-`-based attrs for output HTML tables
description: This further adds more `data-` attribute keys and values to the output HTML table. Allows for better identification of table parts by HTML tag.

title: Base64 functions: rearranging statements and adding #nocov start/end comments
description: This simply adds `#nocov start` and `#nocov end` comments around the `encode_base64()` function.

title: General improvements/fixes to some `fmt_*()` functions
description:
This is focussed on specific `fmt_*()` functions. Description of the proposed changes:

 - fixes an error in obtaining correct negative value representations with parentheses for currency values
- allows for left or right placement of the currency symbol and an option to include a space character between the currency value and the currency symbol
- removes unnecessary `library()` statements from roxygen @examples sections
- visual improvements to statements (e.g., removing line breaks, etc.)

title: Check for availability of the shiny package
description: This modifies the Shiny-based functions so that they always perform an availability check for the `shiny` package. If `shiny` is not present then these functions will `stop()` with a message to obtain `shiny` from CRAN.

title: Documentation fixes for reexported functions
description: For the the reexported functions `dplyr::vars()` and `dplyr::funs()`, extra roxygen documentation sections were removed. Re-documenting was causing `R CMD Check` warnings and this will remove those warnings.

title: Adding testthat tests for the bulk of the `tab_*()` functions
description: This is a single testing script that focusses on the `tab_*()` functions.

title: Adding tests for all `fmt*()` functions
description: A set of **testthat** tests for all of the `fmt*()` functions is to be added here.

title: Modify tests based on `opts_df` object
description: Some simple fixes to existing `testthat` tests that resolve changes to the `opts_df` data frame (its dimensions).

title: docs: fix some typos
description:
# Summary

docs: fix some typos

title: fix: `gt_split()` fails with grouped df
description:
This PR addresses a bug in the `gt_split()` function where splitting a grouped data frame could result in incorrect or stale row group metadata. The fix ensures that each split table only contains the relevant row groups present in its data. Additionally, some tests have been added to verify correct behavior when splitting grouped tables.

Fixes: https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/2089

title: fix: LaTeX renders incorrectly when `cols_merge()` uses angle brackets
description:
This PR addresses a bug in the `cols_merge()` function where using `<<`/`>>` patterns could produce corrupted output if data values contained `<` or `>` characters, especially in LaTeX output. The update ensures that angle brackets in data values are handled safely during pattern processing. Additional tests are included to verify the fix, and documentation is updated accordingly.

Fixes: https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/2153

title: feat: add option to remove leading zero from some numeric formatters
description:
This PR introduces a new `drop_leading_zero` argument to several numeric formatting functions in the package. This option allows users to remove the leading zero from numbers between -1 and 1 (e.g., `0.75` becomes `.75`), which is useful for displaying statistics like correlations and p-values. The change is applied consistently across formatting functions, documentation, and internal helpers.

Fixes: https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/2146

title: Xml pptx
description:

Thank you for contributing to **gt**! To make this process easier for everyone, please explain the context and purpose of your contribution. Also, list the changes made to the existing code or documentation.

title: fix: `text_replace()` in LaTeX should operate on non-escaped text
description:
This PR improves the consistency of text replacement and transformation functions in both HTML and LaTeX/PDF table outputs, particularly for patterns containing LaTeX special characters. It introduces a mechanism to decode and re-escape LaTeX special characters for plain-text operations, ensuring that functions like `text_replace()` work the same way in both output formats.

Fixes: https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/1592

title: fix: make `text_transform()` safely unescape certain HTML entities after the transformation is applied
description:
This PR fixes an issue with `text_transform()` where user-supplied functions were receiving HTML-escaped text (such as `&`) instead of the original display text. Now, transformation functions receive plain text, ensuring that string operations behave as expected.

Fixes: https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/2033

title: fix: `md()` used with column in LaTeX
description:
This PR addresses a rendering issue in LaTeX/PDF output where using `md()` with a column label caused the column to expand to the full page width when no explicit column width was set. The fix ensures that such labels no longer trigger `\parbox{\linewidth}` in the LaTeX output, and adds corresponding tests to prevent regressions.

Fixes: https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/2124

title: fix: row groups unintentionally merging
description:
This PR fixes a bug where multi-column stub rowspans could incorrectly cross row-group boundaries if adjacent groups shared the same stub value, causing group labels to appear in the wrong rows. The fix now ensures that rowspans for stub columns are restricted within their respective row groups.

Fixes: https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/2121

title: Fix column spanners not displaying correctly with multi-column stub
description:
# Summary

This PR fixes a minor bug in `create_columns_component_h`: In the multi-column stub branch, `colspan` was incorrectly set to `length(stub_layout)` (which always seems to be `1`) but should be `get_stub_column_count(data)`, the number of stub columns present. This minor change resolves the below-mentioned issue.

# Related GitHub Issues and PRs

- Ref: #2170

- [x] I have listed any major changes in the [NEWS](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/NEWS.md).
- [x] I have added [`testthat`](https://github.com/r-lib/testthat) unit tests to [`tests/testthat`](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/tree/master/tests/testthat) for any new functionality.

title: Fix resolve_hierarchical_stub_indices matching wrong group leader
description:
# Summary

`resolve_hierarchical_stub_indices()` contains a bug, resulting in group leaders being determined incorrectly when cell labels repeat in non-contiguous groups. The PR fixes this by searching for the group leader starting at `row_idx` upwards until a different group is encountered -- instead of starting in the first row and searching downwards for the first match, which can be an unrelated, non-adjacant group further up the table.

# Related GitHub Issues and PRs

- Ref: #2168

- [x] I have added [`testthat`](https://github.com/r-lib/testthat) unit tests to [`tests/testthat`](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/tree/master/tests/testthat) for any new functionality.

title: Fix grand summaries with multicolumn stubs
description:
# Summary

This fixes the rendering of grand summary rows when multiple columns are supplied to `rowname_col`.

The HTML renderer now uses the actual number of stub columns to:

* prevent recycling between the summary data and rendered table cells
* span the grand-summary label across all stub columns
* keep the calculated value aligned under its intended data column

A regression test reproduces the two-column example and verifies that `Total` appears once, `210` appears under `Count`, and the label cell has the correct colspan.

# Related GitHub issues and PRs

* Fixes #2164

# Testing

* Added a regression test in `test-multicolumn_stub.R`
* `git diff --check` passes
* The test suite was not run locally because R is unavailable in the Codespace; CI will perform runtime validation

* [x] I have listed any major changes in the [[NEWS](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/NEWS.md)](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/NEWS.md).
* [x] I have added [[testthat](https://github.com/r-lib/testthat)](https://github.com/r-lib/testthat) unit tests to [`[tests/testthat](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/tree/master/tests/testthat)`](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/tree/master/tests/testthat) for any new functionality.
